title: schema.prisma Structure
description: Master the structure of the schema.prisma file, including datasource, generators, models, and environment variable configuration.

data.text: The `schema.prisma` file is the central source of truth for your entire application's data tier. It uses Prisma's custom modeling language (Prisma Schema Language / PSL) to describe data sources, output generators, database models, enums, and relations in a clean, human-readable format.

data.title: Top-Level Schema Components
items: **`datasource` block**: Specifies which database provider to connect to (e.g. `postgresql`, `mysql`, `sqlite`) and passes the database connection URL.
**`generator` block**: Defines what artifacts to generate when running `prisma generate` (most commonly `prisma-client-js`).
**`model` blocks**: Define the structure of your application entities, mapping directly to tables or collections in your database.

data.text: Modern cloud PostgreSQL providers like Neon and Supabase use connection poolers (such as PgBouncer) to support thousands of concurrent serverless functions. However, schema migrations (`prisma migrate dev` or `prisma migrate deploy`) require direct, session-level database access because PgBouncer in transaction mode does not support advisory locks or prepared statements. Prisma allows defining `directUrl` specifically for CLI migrations while using `url` for pooled application queries.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `schema.prisma` is the single source of truth for the database and TypeScript types.
Use `env()` to inject connection secrets securely without hardcoding credentials.
Configure `directUrl` alongside `url` when deploying on serverless architectures using PgBouncer or Neon.
